concept.title: DualArrayDeque 再平衡的摊还成本
concept.core_question: 为什么 DualArrayDeque 的线性再平衡成本可以摊还为每次更新 O(1)？
concept.summary: 再平衡后两栈大小几乎相等，再次失衡前需积累 Ω(n) 次更新，足以分摊 O(n) 搬移。
concept.definition: 从空 DualArrayDeque 开始执行 m 次 add 与 remove，所有 balance 重建的总时间为 $O(m)$。可用势能 $\Phi=|front.size()-back.size()|$ 说明：重建后 $\Phi\le1$，单次未重建更新最多让势能增加 1，而触发三倍失衡时势能大于 n/2，因此两次重建之间有与 n 同阶的更新。

relations.description: 理解《DualArrayDeque 再平衡的摊还成本》是继续学习目标知识点的直接基础。

rookie_explanation.analogy: 天平被重新调平后，每次只加减一个砝码，必须经过许多次变化才会再次严重倾斜；调平成本可由这些变化共同承担。
rookie_explanation.boundary: 类比不替代势能不等式证明，也不保证触发重建的单次操作为常数时间。

related_concepts.title: DualArrayDeque 的再平衡
related_concepts.core_question: DualArrayDeque 在什么条件下重新分配 front 与 back 的元素？
related_concepts.summary: 当一侧超过另一侧三倍时，balance 按逻辑顺序重建两栈，使两侧分别约占一半。
related_concepts.definition: 当元素数至少为 2 且 front 与 back 的大小相差超过 3 倍时，DualArrayDeque 的 balance 按逻辑序列重建两个 ArrayStack，使 front 保存前 $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ 个元素并逆序排列，back 保存其余 $\lceil n/2\rceil$ 个元素并正序排列。一次重建移动 $O(n)$ 个元素。

related_concepts.title: DualArrayDeque 的操作复杂度
related_concepts.core_question: DualArrayDeque 是否达到与 ArrayDeque 相同的渐近性能？
related_concepts.summary: 它的 get/set 为 O(1)，按位更新为 O(1+min(i,n-i))，resize 与 balance 总成本均可线性摊还。
related_concepts.definition: DualArrayDeque 实现 List 接口时，get 与 set 为 $O(1)$；忽略内部 resize 和 balance，add(i,x) 与 remove(i) 为 $O(1+\min\{i,n-i\})$。从空结构开始的 m 次更新中，所有 resize 与 balance 总时间为 $O(m)$，渐近性能与 ArrayDeque 相同。

source_records.content: Here there is little to analyze. If the \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} operation does rebalancing, then it moves $O(\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}})$ elements and this takes $O(\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}})$ time. This is bad, since \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} is called with each call to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}}. However, the following lemma shows that, on average, \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} only spends a constant amount of time per operation.

\lemlabel{dualarraydeque-amortized} If an empty DualArrayDeque is created and any sequence of $m\ge 1$ calls to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} are performed, then the total time spent during all calls to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} is $O(m)$.

We will show that, if \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} is forced to shift elements, then the number of \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} operations since the last time any elements were shifted by \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} is at least $\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/2-1$. As in the proof of \lemref{arraystack-amortized}, this is sufficient to prove that the total time spent by \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} is $O(m)$. We will perform our analysis using a technique knows as the \emph{potential method}. \index{potential} \index{potential method} Define the \emph{potential}, $\Phi$, of the DualArrayDeque as the difference in size between \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}}} and \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}}}: \[ \Phi = |\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}} - \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}}| \enspace . \] The interesting thing about this potential is that a call to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} or \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} that does not do any balancing can increase the potential by at most 1. Observe that, immediately after a call to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} that shifts elements, the potential, $\Phi_0$, is at most 1, since \[ \Phi_0 = \left|\lfloor\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/2\rfloor-\lceil\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/2\rceil\right|\le 1 \enspace .\] Consider the situation immediately before a call to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} that shifts elements and suppose, without loss of generality, that \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} is shifting elements because $3\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}} < \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}}$. Notice that, in this case, \begin{eqnarray*} \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}} & = & \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}}+\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}} \\ & < & \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}}/3+\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}} \\ & = & \frac{4}{3}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}} \end{eqnarray*} Furthermore, the potential at this point in time is \begin{eqnarray*} \Phi_1 & = & \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}} - \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{front}}.\mathrm{size}()}} \\ &>& \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}} - \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}}/3 \\ &=& \frac{2}{3}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{back}}.\mathrm{size}()}} \\ &>& \frac{2}{3}\times\frac{3}{4}\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}} \\ &=& \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/2 \end{eqnarray*} Therefore, the number of calls to \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{add}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}},\ensuremath{\mathit{x}})}} or \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{remove}(\ensuremath{\mathit{i}})}} since the last time \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathrm{balance}()}} shifted elements is at least $\Phi_1-\Phi_0 > \ensuremath{\ensuremath{\ensuremath{\mathit{n}}}}/2-1$. This completes the proof.
